text: They searched everywhere. <break time="0.8s" /> In the folds of her dress. <break time="0.8s" /> In the folds of her coat. <break time="0.8s" /> And in the pockets. <break time="0.8s" /> But they found nothing. <break time="0.8s" /> Her husband went out again. <break time="0.8s" /> And walked over the whole route. <break time="0.8s" /> They had taken home. <break time="0.8s" /> He went to the police. <break time="0.8s" /> And to the cab companies. <break time="0.8s" /> And he even put an advertisement. <break time="0.8s" /> In the newspapers. <break time="0.8s" /> At the end of a week. <break time="0.8s" /> They had lost all hope. <break time="0.8s" /> And Loisel. <break time="0.8s" /> Who looked five years older. <break time="0.8s" /> Said We must replace the necklace. <break time="0.8s" /> In a shop at the Palais Royal. <break time="0.8s" /> They found a string of diamonds. <break time="0.8s" /> That seemed exactly like the one they had lost. <break time="0.8s" /> It cost forty thousand francs. <break time="0.8s" /> But they could have it. <break time="0.8s" /> For thirty six thousand. <break time="0.8s" /> Loisel had eighteen thousand francs. <break time="0.8s" /> From his father. <break time="0.8s" /> And he borrowed the rest. <break time="0.8s" /> From anyone who would lend it. <break time="0.8s" /> He signed promises to pay. <break time="0.8s" /> Made ruinous agreements. <break time="0.8s" /> And risked the rest of his life. <break time="0.8s" /> When Madame Loisel took the necklace back. <break time="0.8s" /> Madame Forestier said coldly. <break time="0.8s" /> You should have returned it sooner. <break time="0.8s" /> She did not open the box. <break time="0.8s" /> And Madame Loisel. <break time="0.8s" /> Felt a great relief.
